+//! #4153 Trochoidal slot baseline: a 12 mm slot along a straight 20 mm
+//! chain with a Ø6 cutter, the microlift return and the retract return,
+//! climb and conventional, a known stock top, and a 16 mm slot. A curved
+//! chain is not in the set: the old planner refuses the arcs tried (radius
+//! 30, 12 mm wide) with "the centre line turns too tightly".
+
+use super::pin;
+use camcraft_motion::geo2d::Point2;
+use camcraft_motion::machining2d::{TrochoidParams, TrochoidReturn, trochoidal_slot};
+
+fn params() -> TrochoidParams {
+    TrochoidParams {
+        tool_diameter: 6.0,
+        width: 12.0,
+        loop_width: None,
+        step: 1.5,
+        max_engagement: 90.0,
+        ret: TrochoidReturn::Microlift { height: 0.3 },
+        smoothing: 0.5,
+        stock_to_leave: 0.0,
+        clearance_z: 5.0,
+        retract_z: Some(1.0),
+        top_z: 0.0,
+        bottom_z: -4.0,
+        stepdown: 2.0,
+        feed: 800.0,
+        return_feed: 2000.0,
+        plunge_feed: 200.0,
+        climb: true,
+        stock_top: None,
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn kernel_baseline_trochoid_slot() {
+    let straight = [Point2::new(0.0, 0.0), Point2::new(20.0, 0.0)];
+    let cases: [(&str, &[Point2], TrochoidParams); 5] = [
+        ("straight", &straight, params()),
+        ("straight_retract", &straight, TrochoidParams { ret: TrochoidReturn::Retract, ..params() }),
+        ("straight_conventional", &straight, TrochoidParams { climb: false, ..params() }),
+        ("straight_stock_top", &straight, TrochoidParams { stock_top: Some(-1.0), ..params() }),
+        ("wide", &straight, TrochoidParams { width: 16.0, ..params() }),
+    ];
+    for (case, chain, p) in cases {
+        pin("trochoid_slot", case, &trochoidal_slot(chain, &p).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{case}: {e}")));
+    }
+}

+## #4025 - Path kernel K1: one region model for selection, material side and bounds
+
+Stage 1 of the K0 record (`## #4024` in `RECOMMENDED.md`, "Stage 1:
+Region"). The kernel builds one region value with `region(sel, material,
+bounds, plane, tool, leave)`. The motion adapter
+(`crates/motion/src/machining2d/kernel_region.rs`) turns the present region
+inputs into the kernel inputs. No old planner calls the adapter. With the
+planner switch at its default, the output does not change.
+
+**What was decided**
+
+1. **One selection type for all picks.** An edge, a face, a chain and
+   points that straight lines join all become a `Chain` (a polyline, open
+   or closed). A `Selection` holds one or more chains. Nested closed chains
+   are holes. A chain is refused when it has a point that is not finite,
+   too few points, two neighbour points at the same place, all its points
+   on one line (closed), or a self-crossing. A selection is refused when it
+   is empty, or when two chains cross or touch. The crossing test is a
+   sweep over the x-sorted segments. Dropped: a selection enum with one
+   variant for each pick kind (the region law is the same for each kind);
+   a union of crossing chains (the meaning is not clear, so the kernel
+   refuses it by name).
+2. **The meaning of `MaterialSide`.** `Inside` cuts the area that the
+   closed chains enclose (a pocket, a bore, Contour "Inside"). `Outside`
+   cuts the stock round that area (Contour "Outside", the band round a
+   part). The carriers map so: Contour `Side::Inside` and `Side::Outside`
+   map to the same names; `Side::Auto` maps to no side (the caller resolves
+   Auto first); the pocket family is `Inside`; `StartSide::around_part`
+   with the stock known is `Outside` of the part (the part is the stock
+   less the band). `ChainSide` and `Containment` of the area controls are
+   not mapped in K1: they act on open boundaries in `camcraft-app`, and the
+   kernel refuses open chains (decision 3).
+3. **An open chain is refused** (`OPEN_NEEDS_SIDE`): it encloses no area,
+   so it has no inside or outside. This is the record's refusal "a material
+   side that the selection cannot have (an open chain with no side)". The
+   "on the line" region of Trace, Engrave and 2D Chamfer is the work of
+   #3758. `KernelRegion` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so that step can add it.
+4. **The Outside centre reaches the stock outline.** The centre is the
+   stock less the selection grown by the tool radius plus the stock to
+   leave. A loop of the centre whose vertices are all on the stock outline
+   (within 1 um) is a stock edge. Each other loop is a part wall, also a
+   loop with parts of the two (the conservative reading: the tool must not
+   cross it). The air is the band between the stock grown by one tool
+   radius and grown by two radii, less the keep-out: there the disc does
+   not touch the stock. Today the 2D Offset band erodes the whole band, so
+   its centre stays the tool radius plus the stock to leave inside the
+   stock outline. The pin
+   `the_offset_band_keeps_off_the_stock_edge_and_the_kernel_reaches_it`
+   names this difference. The part walls agree within the arc tolerance
+   of the polygon offset: the band erodes the part's hole and the kernel
+   grows the part, which gives two chord sets of one arc (4.8 um apart on
+   the pin's part, the offset's arc tolerance is 5 um). Dropped: erode the stock
+   outline by the radius (the disc then leaves the convex stock corners
+   uncut, at the radius times the square root of 2); erode it by the radius
+   plus the stock to leave (that also leaves a skin of stock at an edge
+   that has no part).
+   **Decided by the maintainer** (question dialog, 2026-11-26): "Yes, to
+   the edge". For the material side Outside, the tool centre can go to
+   the stock outline. The cutter overhangs the stock by up to one tool
+   radius. A clamp at the stock edge needs a keep-out.
+5. **The Inside centre is the exact erosion.** The centre is the selection
+   eroded by the tool radius plus the stock to leave. It is not clipped to
+   the stock, and it has no air: it is a closed area. The kernel keeps a
+   very small piece of centre. Today the Pocket path drops a piece of 0.01
+   mm2 or less (#2232); Contour Inside keeps it. The pin
+   `the_pocket_drops_a_sliver_that_contour_and_the_kernel_keep` names this
+   difference. The guide stage's completeness guard (0.1 mm2, record stage
+   2) decides what is cut. Dropped: the sliver filter in stage 1 (a region
+   is a pure geometric value; a filter there hides area from the guard).
+6. **The keep-out is a part wall.** The centre keeps the tool radius from
+   the keep-out (not the stock to leave: that applies to the part). Its
+   loops are part walls.
+7. **The stock to leave** is finite and greater than minus the tool radius
+   (`BAD_LEAVE`). A negative value is accepted above that limit, as for
+   an undersize finish.
+8. **The bounds refusals.** `Outside` needs the stock (`NEEDS_STOCK`). A
+   selection that does not meet a known stock is refused on each side
+   (`OFF_STOCK`). An `Outside` selection that covers the stock has no
+   material (`EMPTY_MATERIAL`). A tool that does not fit, or a keep-out
+   that covers the centre, gives `EMPTY_CENTER`.
+9. **A region is planned in the plane of its recipe.** `PlanarRegion`
+   holds its `WorkPlane`, and `region` takes it. The 2D coordinates are
+   along the plane's own axes. The pin
+   `a_region_is_planned_in_the_plane_of_its_recipe_not_in_xy` builds a
+   region in the lathe's Z-X plane.
+10. **`PlanarRegion::new` checks the partition and the orientation.** Each
+    loop of the centre is exactly one part wall or one stock edge, in the
+    same direction (any start vertex). The loops of the centre are oriented
+    by their nesting. The orientation check is a guard: `camcraft-geometry`
+    gives only normalized regions, so no public value can break it, and no
+    negative test can reach it. `region` makes the centre normal again when
+    the guard finds a fault.
+11. **`StartSide::around_part` stays on `StartSide` in K1.** The record
+    moves it into the region in K1. The old planners read the field, and
+    the old planners must not change on the side branch. The adapter maps
+    it into the region now. The field goes with the old planners (record
+    step RM).
+12. **The tool is a `ToolShape`, not a radius** (record "What phase 1 keeps
+    open", point 8). The caller gives the shape: the motion parameters have
+    no flute length, so the adapter does not make one up.
+
+**Why**: the record fixes the signature, the invariants and the refusals
+of stage 1, but not the reading of the stock edge, the open chain, the
+carriers' names or the sliver filter. The choices above keep each value
+of the crate valid by construction (#4055 decision 12) and keep the old
+planners as they are.
+
+**Dropped**: see each item. Also dropped: a test in `camcraft-app` through
+`selection_region` (the app's present path). The motion pins compare the
+present centre functions of the same kinds (`non_sliver_center`,
+`prepare_band`) and are lower in the crate graph.
+
+**Cost to change later**: low. The region is internal to the kernel and to
+the adapter. No project file and no posted program changes. A different
+stock-edge reading changes `region_build.rs` and two pins.

+## #4026 - Path kernel K3: the load control stage
+
+Stage 3 (load control) of the K0 record (`## #4024` in `RECOMMENDED.md`).
+Sub-PR of `side/path-kernel`, on top of K4 (#4177). No old planner changes
+and no planner calls the new code yet: with the default switch the output
+is identical.
+
+**What was decided**
+
+1. **Files.** `crates/pathkernel/src/load/`: `law.rs` (the engagement
+   law), `stage.rs` (`LoadStage`, the planner), `rings.rs` (constant
+   engagement), `trochoid.rs` (trochoidal loops). `load.rs` keeps the
+   types. The kernel still depends on `camcraft-geometry` only; no
+   geometry function was added.
+2. **One law for every mode.** The stage makes a raster of the stock
+   reader (`StockRead`, 20 cells across the tool radius, at most 4
+   million cells; a cell that the reader does not know is material, so a
+   read can only be too high). It walks the curves in the cut order, 8
+   reads across the tool radius, and reads each place before it clears
+   the tool disc there. The read is the contact angle phi on the front
+   half of the cutting edge, as ae/D = (1 - cos phi) / 2 (Altintas 2000;
+   Stori & Wright 2000). The read comes after the tool disc at the place
+   is cleared, three quarters of a cell outside the edge, as the #4154
+   meter reads. The first form read half a cell inside the edge before
+   the clear: the disc of the read before had then cleared the side of
+   the arc, and an outward ring read 54 degrees where the geometry gives
+   64 (the meter of #4154 found 2297 unnamed moves on the disc). The
+   stage does not see the entry (stage 5 comes after it), so the first
+   cut is read without the bore of its entry: it can be named where the
+   entry clears its start. A read can be too high, not too low. Every curve is read, the clean-up rings too: the
+   law of #3849 (PR #4008 checks the clean-up passes as the lanes) holds
+   by construction, because no curve is skipped.
+3. **A stated limit for a choice without one.** `LoadControl::None` and
+   `Trochoidal` carry no engagement. `LoadStage::new(limit)` states the
+   limit that the stage names cuts against; the default is 0.5 (a 90
+   degree contact, the old default trochoid limit). A kind sets it to its
+   planned load (for rings: stepover / D). Dropped: a limit field on
+   `LoadControl::None` (it changes a public type that the other stages
+   and the kit build).
+4. **None is the identity.** The set is the input set (marks included);
+   each read above `limit x (1 + PLAN_TOL)` gets an over-limit record with
+   the reason `NO_CONTROL`, and the verdict has one status line note for
+   each reason (the count, the worst load and its place). `Controlled::new`
+   stays the single gate: an unnamed read above the limit is refused.
+5. **Constant engagement on rings inserts passes.** Where a ring reads
+   above the load, the stage finds the nearest curve cut before it at
+   the hot place. When both are rings of one distance field (the walls of
+   the centre area, or the part walls of a region with a stock edge: the
+   distance of each point agrees within 1 % of the tool radius), it
+   inserts the mid level of that field between them, only the pieces
+   within the gap of the hot ring, turned to run as that ring runs. It
+   reads the plan again, at most 12 rounds and at most 8 times the curves
+   (and 64). An insertion is kept only when it lowers the load of its ring
+   (no hot read left, or the worst excess halved, or a quarter of the hot
+   reads gone); else it is taken out and the ring is named `NOT_FIXED`.
+   That is the sharp corner of offset rings (the #3933 rectangle read
+   93.9 %): more passes do not help there, the corner is named, not
+   hidden, and the note names Adaptive. A ring with no earlier curve
+   within one diameter is `FRESH_CUT` (the first ring of a pocket), a
+   curve that is no ring is `NOT_A_RING`, a gap below 2 x 15 % of the load
+   width is `AT_FLOOR` (the floor of the held #3933 design). A
+   `FullWidth` mark with no hot read left is resolved and removed; a mark
+   that stays is named by its reads.
+   Dropped: the outward spiral and the morph of #3933 (Held & Spielberger
+   2009). A spiral is a link and an entry matter (record: load control
+   adds no link). Dropped too: a new spacing of the whole ladder by the
+   Stori & Wright law (fewer passes than a mid-level insertion, which
+   halves a gap). The insertion reads the true stock at each step, so it
+   is correct for any ring shape; the cost is more passes than an
+   optimal ladder.
+6. **The stock reach stays with the HSM planner.**
+   `ConstantEngagement { reach: Stock }` (Adaptive) is refused by this
+   stage with `STOCK_REACH_ELSEWHERE`: the K0 record revision 2 keeps the
+   HSM planner in `camcraft-motion` behind the load trait. So Offset
+   rings (Rings) and Adaptive (Stock) stay two behaviours, as the
+   maintainer answered (3).
+7. **Trochoidal replaces each full-width stretch.** Each `FullWidth`
+   stretch is cut as loops that walk the stretch itself (#3932: the path
+   follows the contour and does not slot to a wall). A loop is
+   `q + rho n (1 - cos t) + rho d sin t`: it leaves the stretch and comes
+   back to it, one loop a step. Its radius is the room on the side with
+   more room (the largest disc that touches the stretch there and lies in
+   the centre area), at most half the loop width; so a loop cannot leave
+   the area, and a point outside it is refused (`LOOP_LEAVES`). The step
+   is the trochoid pitch, at most the load width of the stated limit
+   (the front arc of a loop cuts about one step: Otkur & Lazoglu 2007,
+   Rauch, Duc & Hascoet 2009). A loop with less room than 5 % of the tool
+   radius is cut as the stretch: where no loop fits, the stretch stays and
+   its reads are named `NO_ROOM`. Reads above the limit on the loops are
+   `LOOPS_OVER`, on other curves `NOT_MARKED`. The marks of a changed
+   curve go (their reads name what stays). A closed curve keeps the
+   start that the order stage gave it.
+   Dropped: a microlift return between loops (a link matter; the kernel's
+   hop is stage 5); the loop sense from climb or conventional (the loop
+   runs forward on the stretch, as the ring runs).
+
+**Readings** (measured, not tuned).
+
+The law suite (`tests/laws/load_stage.rs`; the check grid of the suite
+walks the plan; hot = a read above `load x 1.05`):
+
+| Fixture (load) | None: curves, hot reads, worst | Constant engagement: curves, hot reads (unnamed), worst |
+|---|---|---|
+| disc pocket (0.25) | 4, 3, 0.413 | 9, 0 (0), 0.179 |
+| pocket with an island (0.20) | 12, 286, 0.999 | 29, 146 (0), 0.998 |
+| two lobes and a neck (0.40) | 9, 249, 0.998 | 27, 128 (0), 0.998 |
+
+The island and the neck keep their full-width first rings and their
+sharp corners: named (`FRESH_CUT`, `AT_FLOOR`). Trochoidal on the neck:
+the worst read in the marked stretch is 0.941 (was a full-width 1.0);
+the loops stay in the centre area.
+
+Motion `kernel_laws::k3_load` (the #4154 measures, limit 60 degrees,
+25 % load, the band round the part): feed moves above the limit, the
+worst in degrees, and the moves above the limit with no named place
+within one tool radius.
+
+| Case | Old 2D Pocket | Kernel, None | Kernel, constant engagement |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| disc Inside | 20, 178 | 3507, 173, 0 | 833, 173, 1 |
+| disc Outside | 20, 178 | 402, 145, 13 | 334, 118, 74 |
+| dog bone Inside | 32, 180 | 2587, 173, 0 | 581, 173, 1 |
+| dog bone Outside | 32, 180 | 724, 167, 3 | 678, 143, 66 |
+
+The kernel counts every short move of its dense rings (the old planner
+has fewer, longer moves), so the counts are not one to one. The worst
+Inside (173) is the first ring round the part: full width, named. The
+unnamed moves Outside are on the stock edge line, where a piece starts
+after a lift: there the kernel read and the #4154 meter differ. That is
+follow-up #4260 (P7). The one unnamed move Inside is a link feed (stage 5).
+
+**Cost of a change later.** A new spacing law is one function in
+`rings.rs` behind the same reads. A tool shape other than a disc changes
+only the edge read in `law.rs`.

+## #4027 - Path kernel K7: the law suite and its stand-in proofs
+
+**What was decided**
+
+1. **The suite is the existing directory suite `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/`.**
+   The issue text says "an existing directory suite"; the K0 record says
+   `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/`. The record is the approved design, and
+   the crate skeleton (#4055, PR #4123) already made `tests/laws.rs` with
+   its invariant tests and wrote that "the K7 law suite (#4027) joins this
+   directory suite". So the two texts agree: K7 adds submodules to the one
+   binary `laws`, and adds no new top-level test file. No xtask list
+   changes: the gate already maps `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/` to that
+   binary.
+2. **One generic check for each law.** Each check is a function over the
+   stage traits (`GuidePlanner`, `OrderPlanner`, `LoadPlanner`,
+   `LinkProof`, `EntryPlanner`) and the stage outputs of one run. It
+   returns a `LawVerdict`: the law, held or broken, and the worst measure
+   (its place, its point, its measured value and its limit).
+   - L1 `check_l1`: two calls, the region given another way (loops
+     reversed, each started at its next vertex), and each guide planner of
+     another kind with the same choice. Curve multisets within 1 um
+     (Hausdorff per curve, same count).
+   - L2 `check_l2`: compile-level (a region stage is a
+     `fn(MaterialSide) -> ...`), then the centre changes with the material
+     side, and the order stage gives the same sequence for two regions that
+     differ only in their material side.
+   - L3 `check_l3`: Auto, Inside and Outside; the ordered curves against
+     the guide curves, and the guide and the ordered multiset across the
+     sides, within 1 um.
+   - L4 `check_l4`: a guide family other than the asked one, or an entry
+     into material of another kind than the asked one, needs a named
+     fallback of its stage.
+   - L5 `check_l5`, L6 `check_l6`: read on a stock grid that the checks own
+     (`grid.rs`), written apart from the planner's stock reader. The walk
+     reads each entry and each cut on the stock as it is at that step and
+     clears the swept disc. L5: a descent onto material needs an
+     `IntoMaterial` proof. L6: the engagement is read from the contact
+     angle of the front half of the cutting edge, `ae/D = (1 - cos angle) / 2`
+     (the record names the contact-angle law). Each read above
+     `limit x (1 + PLAN_TOL)` plus the grid read error (0.1 ae/D) needs an
+     over-limit record within one tool radius. The first version of the
+     check found a real under-read of the first stand-in load planner at
+     the corners of sharp offset rings (ae/D 0.75 against the limit 0.5).
+     A hand estimate of the contact angle there gives about 0.77. The
+     stand-in now names the corners.
+   - L7 `check_l7`: the cuts in order, point by point, against the
+     recorded old output, within 1 um. A case with no record is a breach,
+     so that no kind moves without its golden output.
+   - Link rule `check_link`: the plan's lifts against the tally (total and
+     by reason), no lift on a fixture with no split ring, and no stay-down
+     hop that leaves the centre area and the air.
+3. **The mutation proof uses stand-in planners in the test.** No kind has
+   a kernel planner yet. `standins.rs` holds one planner set that obeys
+   each law (sharp offset rings, a side order, a load reader, a straight
+   link, a helix entry). Each law file holds one or more planners that
+   break its law in one named way, and a test that the check names the law
+   and the place. The stand-ins are test code, not a design of K2-K5.
+4. **The registry is the progress list.** `registry.rs` holds the 16
+   phase-1 kinds of the record, each `NotYet`. A kind that moves sets its
+   row to `Moved` and registers its recipe (planners and cases); the test
+   `each_moved_kind_obeys_every_law` then runs `check_all` (all eight
+   checks) on each case. The guard test fails with a clear message when a
+   row is `Moved` with no recipe, or has a recipe and is not `Moved`. The

+## #4055 - The path kernel crate skeleton, the stage types and the planner switch
+
+The dependency decision of the new edges (`camcraft-pathkernel` ->
+`camcraft-geometry`, `camcraft-motion` -> `camcraft-pathkernel`) is the
+record `docs/decisions/4024-path-kernel-design.md` ("Dependency
+decision"). This file holds only the choices that the record left open
+for this step.
+
+**What was decided**
+
+1. **The switch value is parsed in the crate, read in the app.**
+   `PlannerEngine`, `PLANNER_ENV` and `engine_from_switch` are in
+   `camcraft-pathkernel` (`engine.rs`): pure values, so the later
+   comparison harness and the kind PRs use the same parse. The one reader
+   of the process setting is `planner_engine()` in
+   `crates/app/src/operation/planner_switch.rs`. It reads the setting one
+   time for each process (`OnceLock`) and logs a bad value one time. Tests
+   pass the engine directly to `check_engine(kind, engine)`.
+2. **The switch is applied in `run_job`, before every arm**, not in each of
+   the 16 match arms. Under "new", each phase-1 kind is refused with
+   "the new path planner does not plan <kind> yet (CAMCRAFT_PLANNER=new)".
+   A kind PR adds its kernel route there. A kind outside phase 1 keeps its
+   planner under either value: the switch does not cover it.
+3. **Accepted values**: unset, empty or `old` (any case) give the old
+   planner; `new` or `kernel` give the kernel. Each other value gives the
+   old planner and one diagnostic that names the value.
+4. **The Order stage has its own `StartSide { Auto, Inside, Outside }`.** The
+   record names motion's `PassStart`, but the crate must not import motion.
+   Motion converts `PassStart` into `StartSide`, as it converts `Links`
+   into `LinkPolicy`.
+5. **`EntryChoice.asked` is an `EntryKind`**, not motion's `Entry3D`, for
+   the same reason.
+6. **One file for each stage now** (`guide.rs`, `load.rs`, `entry.rs`), not
+   the record's directories (`guide/{rings,..}.rs`). A directory comes with
+   its first planner (K2, K3, K5), because an empty file is noise.
+7. **The step law of a plan is a transition table** (`Plan::new`, #4123
+   review finding 2). The states are clear, ready, cut end and lifted. A
+   cut consumes the readiness, so each cut needs its own entry or
+   stay-down link. A lift must be followed by an entry. The plan must end
+   clear (after an exit, or empty). The table is in the doc comment of
+   `Plan::new`, and the suite tests each cell.
+8. **The pin `switch_default_is_the_old_planner` is a heavy-lane test.** It
+   generates the 2D Offset Inside on `fig8.step` through the dispatch and
+   compares it with the #3750 golden `offset2d_fig8_inside.cl`. One fig8
+   generation runs past the 60 s debug budget, as the #3750 pins do. Two
+   fast pins in the default suite check the switch itself:
+   `switch_default_passes_each_phase1_kind_to_the_old_planner` and
+   `switch_new_refuses_a_kind_it_does_not_plan_yet`. The 2D Pocket has no
+   app-level golden in the baseline. Its rings are pinned by the motion
+   goldens `pocket_band_*` (`pocket_rings_unchanged_by_the_shared_planner`),
+   and the switch passes the Pocket kind to the same arm.
+9. **A test checks the gate lists against the workspace members**
+   (`the_gate_lists_name_every_workspace_crate`, xtask), as the record asks.
+   It pins: the root members equal `ALL_CRATES`; `BATCH_CRATES` is
+   `ALL_CRATES` without `ui`; `CLIPPY` is `ALL_CRATES` without `kernel` (as
+   before this change).
+
+10. **The quick-plan pin follows the gate maps.** The issue asks that
+   `gate quick` on a diff in the new crate lists the crate's suites and
+   the `motion` and `app` suites that depend on it. The quick gate selects
+   suites of another crate only by their Gate map; it has no
+   reverse-dependency fan-out (as for `kernel`). No motion code calls the
+   kernel yet, so no motion suite can name a kernel module truthfully. The
+   app suite `offset_pass_start` names `pathkernel::engine` (its switch
+   pins use it). The xtask pin
+   `a_pathkernel_change_plans_its_suites_and_the_mapped_app_suite` checks
+   this. Each kind PR that makes motion call the kernel names the kernel
+   module in its motion suite's Gate map. A change to `Cargo.toml` or
+   `Cargo.lock` (as in this PR) still makes quick a batch. Dropped: adding
+   the crate to `SHARED` (the record says no) and a fan-out rule for every

+   #3750 baseline goldens (`offset2d_fig8_*.cl`, cherry-picked from

+   notes and warnings that the pins compare).

+    finding 3). A value of a public type is always valid. A field that
+    could hold an invalid value is private and is set only by a checked
+    constructor. An enum variant with data holds a validated newtype
+    (`PlanarFrame`, `Disc`, `RingsChoice`, `RowsChoice`, `TraceOffset`,
+    `Trochoid`, `ConstantLoad`, `StayPath`, `LiftReason`, `Area`, `Hole`,
+    `Spot`, `Positive`, `Engagement`, `Gaps`). A list in a value holds only
+    validated records, and its constructor checks the rules between them.
+    The only public fields left are of types whose every value is valid
+    (`OrderChoice`). `Refusal` maps a blank reason to `NO_REASON` and drops
+    a place that is not finite, so the error type is valid too. Dropped: a
+    `validate()` call at each boundary (it relies on each boundary
+    remembering it, which is the class of the finding).
+13. **The order stage may only restart or reverse a curve** (finding 1).
+    `Curve::same_cut`: same index, family, closure and circle (within the
+    tolerance); a closed curve is a cyclic shift of the input or of its
+    reverse; an open curve is the input or its reverse. The start point of
+    `OrderedSet` must be the first point of its first curve.
+14. **Each proof names its place, and the descent stays in it** (finding
+    4). `Proof::InAir(Area)`, `InColumn(Area)`, `InHole(Hole)` and
+    `IntoMaterial { area, angle_or_pitch }`. The entry has approach moves
+    (above the material, not bound) and descent moves (bound). A descent
+    move is inside the proved area within the tolerance, or, for a hole, no
+    farther from the centre than the hole radius less the tool radius. A
+    hole proof must name one of the holes of the choice (centre and
+    radius).
+15. **Every record in every list is validated** (finding 5). The limit is
+    an engagement in (0, 1]; a reading and an over-limit record are valid
+    by their types (finite place, engagement in [0, 1], a reason that is
+    not blank). Each reading above the limit is named exactly once, and
+    each over-limit record agrees with a reading above the limit (same
+    place and load within the tolerance).
+16. **The guide set has a total order** (finding 6): index, family, open
+    before closed, the canonical point sequence, then the circle. A closed
+    curve starts at its lowest point (the least sequence among equal lowest
+    points); an open curve runs from its lesser end. A curve of zero length
+    and a closed curve that repeats its first point are refused.
+17. **The tests of the invariants use the public API**, in the directory
+    suite `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws.rs` (one submodule for each
+    stage). The record puts the K7 law suite in that directory, so K7
+    joins it. The engine parse keeps its unit tests.
+
+**Why**: the record fixes the place and the default of the switch, but not
+how a test sets it, and not where the 16 kinds are listed. One check
+before the arms keeps the old arms byte-for-byte unchanged.
+
+**Dropped**: a field on `GenJob` (it reaches every caller of `collect_job`,

+value would log on each generation).
+
+**Cost to change later**: low. The switch-over PR changes the default in
+`PlannerEngine::default()`; the removal PR deletes `planner_switch.rs`

+## #4176 - Path kernel K2, second part: the medial line, the trace and the helix guide planners
+
+Stage 2 of the K0 record (`## #4024` in `RECOMMENDED.md`, "Stage 2: Guide
+curves"), second of two sub-PRs. The first part (PR #4189,
+`4176-kernel-guides-rings-rows.md`) gave the ring and the row planners.
+This part gives the medial line, the trace of a chain and the helix (with
+the exact circle rings of a hole). No old planner changes, and no planner
+calls the new code yet: with the default switch the output is identical.
+
+**What was decided**
+
+1. **Files.** `crates/pathkernel/src/guide/`: `medial.rs`, `trace.rs`,
+   `helix.rs` (the helix and the exact circle rings), `lead.rs` (the lead
+   of a helix curve and its checked constructor) and `choice.rs` (the
+   guide choices, moved out of `guide.rs` with no change, so that
+   `guide.rs` stays under 400 lines; the public paths stay the same by
+   re-export). In `camcraft-geometry`, three new files of `geo2d/`:
+   `delaunay.rs` (crate-private), `medial.rs` (`Region::medial_axis`) and
+   `side_offset.rs` (`offset_side`). They are new files, so that the
+   geometry change of K4 (#4177) merges without a conflict except the
+   module list of `geo2d.rs`. No new dependency edge between our crates.
+2. **The medial line is the medial axis of the cutter-centre area** (Blum
+   1967). camcraft-geometry had no medial function. The axis is computed
+   as the Voronoi diagram of points sampled on the boundary (Brandt and
+   Algazi 1992), as the duals of the Delaunay edges (Bowyer 1981, Watson
+   1981, with the visibility walk of Devillers et al. 2002). A Voronoi
+   edge is kept when its two triangles have their centres inside the area
+   and its two boundary points subtend 60 degrees or more at it (the
+   theta-medial axis, Attali and Montanvert 1996, Foskey et al. 2003).
+   - The sample spacing is `sqrt(8 * tol * 0.25 mm)`, so the axis is
+     within the tolerance where the clearance is 0.25 mm or more.
+   - Each branch is simplified by Ramer-Douglas-Peucker at half the
+     tolerance.
+   - Side branches shorter than four sample spacings are sampling noise.
+     They are left out and their count is named in a note.
+   - The samples are sorted before the triangulation, so the axis
+     depends on the boundary point set only, not on the loop order or
+     the start vertex (law 1, pinned).
+   - Why 60 degrees: the centre line of a slot subtends 180 degrees and
+     the branch into a 90-degree corner subtends 90. The branches of a
+     flattened arc (corners flatter than 120 degrees) are noise.
+   - Each branch is a curve of family `Medial`, index 0. A branch round
+     a hole is closed. The verdict is done; the uncut area beside the
+     line is named in a note (new `Ask::Line` of the one guard
+     `cover::judge`), because a centre line does not clear an area.
+   - Dropped: a port of the old `adaptive/medial.rs` spine. It averages
+     the two sides of one channel and refuses any other shape (an
+     island, a fork). The medial axis gives each branch and keeps the
+     clearance radius of each point for later stages (V-Carve depth,
+     the trochoidal width).
+   - Dropped: a straight skeleton (it differs from the medial axis at a
+     reflex corner, so the tool would not be centred).
+3. **Medial refusals.**
+   - `NO_MEDIAL`: no branch is longer than the tolerance. A round area
+     has a centre point, not a line.
+   - `NARROW_NECK`: a piece of the area is narrower than the tolerance
+     at a point, or touches itself. The test is the topology of the
+     erosion by half the tolerance: the piece splits, or one of its
+     holes opens. A test on the sampled clearance radius cannot see a
+     neck that is narrower than the sample spacing, so it was dropped.
+   - `MEDIAL_TOO_FINE`: more than 200000 boundary samples.
+   - `NOT_MEDIAL`, and `NOT_AN_AREA` for the chains of a trace.
+4. **The trace needs a region that holds the chains.** The region of an
+   area (K1) refuses an open chain (it has no material side), and its
+   part walls are cutter-centre loops, not the selection. So a new
+   variant `KernelRegion::Chains(ChainRegion)` holds the picked chains,
+   the work plane, the tool and the keep-out area. It has no material
+   side and no start side. `chain_region(sel, plane, tool, keep_out)`
+   builds it. `KernelRegion` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, and the record says
+   that a later phase adds a region that is not a planar area as a new
+   variant. `KernelRegion::chains()` and `KernelRegion::tool()` are new.
+   The planners of an area refuse a chain region by name (`NOT_AN_AREA`).
+   The kernel's entry stage refuses it today (`NOT_PLANAR` of
+   `entry::stage`), so a trace cannot run through all stages yet. That is
+   owed to the entry stage before the switch-over (follow-up issue #4236).
+   Dropped: the chain in the guide choice (`GuideChoice` is `Copy`, and
+   the chain is region data with its plane); a planar region round the
+   chain (it would hide the chain behind an area).
+5. **Trace offset.** `TraceOffset` above zero is the left of the chain in
+   its point order, below zero the right, zero the chain itself.
+   - A closed chain is read counter-clockwise, so its left is its
+     inside. One rule gives the same curve for either pick direction
+     (pinned).
+   - A closed chain is offset as its area (`Region::offset_fine`, round
+     joins at the tolerance).
+   - An open chain uses the new `offset_side` of camcraft-geometry: the
+     boundary of the disc sweep of the chain (the Minkowski sum), less
+     the end caps and the other side. The parts that the chain comes
+     back over are trimmed (the global invalid loops of Tiller and
+     Hanson 1984). An offset that splits into pieces is named in a note.
+   - A chain whose offset collapses is named in a note. If all chains
+     collapse, the trace is refused (`TRACE_COLLAPSES`).
+   - The stretches where the tool disc meets the keep-out area (grown by
+     the tool radius) are left out, and their length is named in a
+     note. If the whole trace is in the keep-out area, it is refused
+     (`TRACE_KEPT_OUT`).
+   - Each curve is of family `Trace`, index 0. The trace has no coverage
+     guard: it does not clear an area.
+6. **Exact circle rings of a hole** (Circular, Bore; the old
+   `CIRCLE_NOT_YET` is gone).
+   - A rings choice with a circle goes to the circle rings of
+     `helix.rs`. The circle is the boundary of the cutter-centre area of
+     the hole. The planner refuses an area that is not its disc
+     (`CIRCLE_NOT_REGION`: one loop, each vertex and edge midpoint
+     within the tolerance plus the 5 um offset flattening).
+   - Ring `k` has the radius `circle - first_offset - k * stepover`
+     while it is above the tolerance. This is the same level-set rule as
+     the ring planner.
+   - Each ring carries its exact `Circle` (`Curve::arc`) and a carrier
+     polygon with the least chord count of 8 or more whose sagitta is
+     within the tolerance (#3756: no fixed 256 chords). The guard and
+     the marks read the polygon. A later stage posts the circle.
+   - A clearing choice whose last ring's disc does not reach the centre
+     gets one clean-up circle at half that radius, marked `Fill`.
+   - The full-width marks and the one guard are those of the ring
+     planner, so the guard decides done or incomplete. A ring count
+     names the uncut area in a note.
+   - The refusals of the ring planner apply: `WALL_STRIP_UNCUT`,
+     `NO_RING`, `OFFSET_BELOW_CENTER`, `TOO_MANY_RINGS`,
+     `STEP_ABOVE_DIAMETER`.
+7. **The helix** (Thread, a helical bore).
+   - `GuideChoice::Helix(HelixChoice)` is new: the helix circle (the
+     cutter-centre path), the pitch, the drop below the plan level, and

+
+Stage 4 (order) and stage 5 (link) of the K0 record (`## #4024` in
+`RECOMMENDED.md`). Sub-PR of `side/path-kernel`, on top of K2 part 1
+(#4176). No old planner changes and no planner calls the new code yet:
+with the default switch the output is identical.

+**What was decided**
+

+   `stage.rs`; the planner is `OrderStage`) and
+   `crates/pathkernel/src/link/` (`proof.rs`, `route.rs`; the proof is
+   `LinkStage`). `order.rs` and `link.rs` keep the types. The kernel still
+   depends on `camcraft-geometry` only. Geometry got two public functions
+   with their tests: `geo2d::segments_cross` (a proper crossing, the
+   verifier's crossing test) and `geo2d::segment_gap` (the distance of two
+   segments), and `geo2d::point_segment_distance`.
+2. **The marks go with their curves.** `OrderedSet::new` now moves each
+   mark of the guide set to the index of its curve in the ordered set, and
+   gives a stretch of a reversed curve in the new direction. No planner
+   can drop or move a mark: the constructor does it (valid by
+   construction). The load stage (K3) reads `OrderedSet::marks`.
+3. **A full-width stretch is cut last.** Of the curves that are ready
+   to cut, a curve with a `FullWidth` stretch comes after the others, and
+   a closed curve starts where its longest full-width stretch ends, so
+   that the heavy stretch is the last part of that curve. A curve that is
+   full-width as a whole (a `Span::Whole` mark) also comes after the other
+   ready curves. It has no stretch end, and no point of it is less heavy
+   than another, so it starts as a plain curve: a closed curve at its
+   vertex nearest the tool that the link proves (its first vertex on the
+   first step). A whole mark wins over the stretches of the same curve. Why: by then all
+   that the other curves can clear round it is cleared, and the tool
+   leaves the heavy stretch into cut ground; the link into the curve
+   reaches cleared material, not the heavy cut. The walk's sense is not
+   changed for a mark: the start side owns it (law 3). Dropped: "cut
+   first" (the tool enters the heavy cut straight after a link, with less
+   cleared round it); moving the stretch to another level (it would change
+   the Inside/Outside walk). K3 still reads the load and names or slows
+   the stretch.

+   beyond it, else to Inside (the rule of `ring_side::resolve`, read from
+   the region). The `stock` argument of `order` is not needed for it.

+   pocket the deeper rings lie inward; round a part they lie outward
+   (toward the stock edge). The stage reads it from the region: outward
+   when the deepest rings lie nearer to the stock edge than the first
+   ones. Inside starts at the part wall (round a part) or in the middle (a
+   pocket); Outside starts at the stock edge or at the pocket wall (the
+   maintainer's rule of #3741: the sides differ only in where the tool
+   starts). A single level counts as deepest-first.
+6. **Climb and conventional.** Climb keeps the uncut material on the
+   right of the travel (a clockwise spindle). The uncut side is the deeper
+   side when the deeper rings come later, else the shallower side. A
+   closed ring has the deeper side on its left (a loop of a level area);
+   an open piece of a ring round a part has it away from the part walls.

+## #4178 - Path kernel K5: the entry and exit stage
+
+Stage 6 of the K0 record (`## #4024` in `RECOMMENDED.md`, "Stage 6: Entry
+and exit"). The stage is in `crates/pathkernel/src/entry/` (the record's
+folder: `air`, `hole`, `column`, `material`, `exit`, with `proof`, `room`
+and `stage`). The planner is `EntryStage`. No old planner calls it, so
+the output with the default planner switch does not change.
+
+**What was decided**
+
+1. **The entry returns a verdict, so a fallback has a name** (law 4). The
+   trait is now
+   `fn entry(&self, first: &Cut, r: &KernelRegion, cleared: &Region, e: &EntryChoice) -> Result<Verdict<Entry>, Refusal>`.
+   This is the smallest change that the skeleton allows: the guide and
+   the load stages already return `Result<Verdict<_>, Refusal>`, and
+   `Verdict::Done` holds the fallbacks and the notes. `exit` keeps
+   `Result<Exit, Refusal>`: an exit has no user choice to fall back from.
+   `named(entry, choice, why, notes)` builds the verdict, and
+   `needs_fallback(asked, used)` is the one rule: another kind than asked
+   is a fallback, except that an air entry and an arc lead are one family,
+   and an entry in air, in a hole or in a column where an entry into
+   material was asked is not a fallback (the asked kind applies only where
+   the tool must enter material: the record's order of tries; the same
+   reading as the L4 check of #4027). A planner returns `Err` when no
+   entry fits, never `Verdict::Refused` or `Verdict::Incomplete`.
+   Dropped: a new `EntryOutcome` type (a second result type for one
+   stage); a `fallback` field on `Entry` (an entry would then carry a
+   record of the stage, not of its moves).
+2. **The order of tries.** The asked kind first when it is an entry
+   outside material (so that its fallback reason is true), then air, a
+   pre-drilled hole, a cleared column. An entry into material only when
+   the user asked for a helix, a ramp or a plunge: the asked one, then the
+   other one of helix and ramp, with a named fallback. A plunge is never a
+   fallback: it is tried only when asked, and `Entry::led` refuses it
+   without the user's choice and a tool that can plunge. When nothing fits
+   the stage refuses by name: `NO_SAFE_ENTRY` (no entry into material
+   chosen; fix: pre-drill a hole or select a helix or ramp) or
+   `NO_MATERIAL_ENTRY` (the chosen one does not fit). A cut that starts
+   above the material top is entered straight down in air.
+3. **One gate: `Entry::led`.** `Entry::new` keeps its signature and calls
+   `led` with no lead. An entry has a new optional `Lead`: the moves in
+   the plane at the cut depth from the end of the descent onto the cut
+   (the #3746 arc, the move from a hole or a column). `Lead::new(pts,
+   room)` checks two or more points at one depth and no stretch outside
+   the room that it names; `led` checks that it starts where the descent
+   ends. The descent check of the skeleton is unchanged.
+4. **The legal room of the tool centre** at the cut depth is read from
+   the region of K1: the centre, the air band, and the band of one tool
+   radius outside each stock edge loop (there the disc overhangs the stock
+   but touches no part: a loop all on the stock outline has no part wall),
+   less the keep-out grown by the tool radius, grown by `ROOM_TOL`
+   (0.005 mm, the arc tolerance of the polygon offset). The region has
+   no stock outline of its own; a stock edge loop is its best reading.
+   Where a part touches the stock edge, that loop is a part wall and the
+   band is not added there: the lead then must stay in the centre or the
+   air (safe, it can refuse more).
+5. **The air entry (#3746).** The descent is in the air zone: the air of
+   the region less the places within the approach distance of the centre
+   and the stock band. K1's air band is one tool radius wide (stock + r
+   to stock + 2r), so the approach distance is limited to half the tool
+   radius, with a status line note when it is limited. Then the arc of
+   `ArcChoice` (radius, sweep up to 180 degrees) tangent to the cut at its
+   start, on either side, at the asked radius and then halving (5 tries,
+   as the old code); a straight lead in air back along the arc's tangent
+   where the arc start is not in the zone. The straight lead must not
+   enter the centre area: so an Inside start deep in the band is not
+   entered through uncut material. A smaller radius gives a note. The
+   arc is kept as chord points within the chord tolerance; the exact
+   circle (G2/G3) is not recorded yet.
+6. **The hole entry.** The nearest hole whose centre is in the legal
+   room and whose straight lead to the cut start stays in it. A hole
+   narrower than the tool needs a tool that can plunge (the tool cuts the
+   ring between the hole and its radius). Holes carry no depth: the caller
+   gives only holes that reach the cut depth.
+7. **The cleared column.** `cleared` (the trait's argument) is the area
+   where no stock stands down to the cut depth; the caller fills it from
+   its stock reader (`StockRead`). The column is `cleared` less the tool
+   radius (the whole disc is in cleared material), in the legal room. The
+   cut start serves when it is in the column; else the nearest corner of
+   the column with a straight lead in the legal room.
+8. **Helix and ramp limits are the user's** (`MaterialChoice` on
+   `EntryChoice`, set with `with_material`): one descent angle (above 0
+   and below 90 degrees; default 3, the old `DEFAULT_RAMP_ANGLE`) for the
+   helix and the ramp, and the helix radius (default half the tool
+   radius; at most the tool radius, so the core is cut). The helix passes
+   through the cut start, tangent to the cut, and its circle stays in the
+   legal room; 4 radii (halving). The ramp runs along the whole first cut
+   (laps of a closed cut, forth and back on an open one) at no more than
+   the angle; at most 128 passes and 1024 helix turns (the old caps).
+   Dropped: a separate helix pitch (the angle gives the pitch,
+   2 pi R tan a).
+9. **The exit.** `Exit::proved(last, lead_out, retract, top)`: the
+   lead-out starts at the end of the last cut at its depth, and the
+   retract is at or above the material top (no rapid in material). The
+   lead-out is an arc (the lead-in reversed) in the room where the tool
+   cuts nothing: its disc stays in the cleared area, the band the last
+   cut swept, or the air round the stock. Where none fits, the tool goes
+   straight up. `Exit::new` keeps its signature and builds only an exit
+   with no lead-out; `Some(points)` is refused (`UNPROVED_LEAD_OUT`), so
+   no unproved lead-out can exist.
+10. **The heights are the planner's**, not the choice's: `Heights { top,
+    clear, retract }` along the plane normal, in the depth units of the
+    plan. The descent starts at the top plus the clearance.
+11. **Geometry in `camcraft-geometry`**: `geo2d::arc_points` (an arc as
+    chords within a tolerance, at most 4096 chords) and
+    `Region::holds_path` (no stretch of a polyline outside the region).
+    The kernel keeps no private copy.
+
+**For the law suite (#4027, PR #4175)**: #4175 merged to the side branch
+first, so this PR changes it to the new signature:
+- each stand-in `impl EntryPlanner` returns `Ok(Verdict::done(entry))`
+  (`standins.rs`, `l5_entry.rs`, `l4_fallback.rs`);
+- `kit::Run` gets `entries: Vec<Verdict<Entry>>`, and `kit::run` takes
+  the entry out of its verdict with `live`;
+- `check_l4` counts an entry as silent when `needs_fallback(asked, used)`
+  is true and its verdict has no fallback of `Stage::Entry`. Before, it
+  treated `ArcLead` as an entry into material and could read no record;
+- new pins: `l4_holds_for_a_named_entry_fallback` and
+  `the_entry_stage_passes_l4_and_l5` (the stage on the square and the
+  island cases).
+
+**Why**: the record fixes the order of tries and the laws, but not how a
+fallback is carried, how the room is read from K1's region, or where the
+user's limits live. Each choice keeps every value valid by construction
+(#4055 decision 12) and keeps the old planners as they are.
+
+**Cost to change later**: low. The stage is internal to the kernel; no
+project file and no posted program changes until a kind PR calls it.

+## #4241 - Path kernel K4b: a link can run outside the stock where the ground is proved
+
+Follow-up of K4 (#4177, `docs/decisions/4177-kernel-order-link.md`,
+decision 8). Sub-PR of `side/path-kernel`. No old planner changes and no
+planner calls the new code yet: with the default switch the output is
+identical.
+
+**What was decided**
+
+1. **The edge band is open ground for the part, not for the stock.** A
+   link sample can now stand in the cutter-centre area, in the air, or in
+   the edge band. The edge band is the band outside the stock within one
+   tool radius of a stock edge. The link stage reads it from the legal
+   room of the entry stage (`entry::legal_room`, K5): the centre, the air
+   and the band at the stock edge, less the keep-out grown by the tool
+   radius. There is one definition, not a second one. A sample in the
+   band must also:
+   - not be inside the part zone (see 2), so the disc meets no part;
+   - be more than a tool radius from each keep-out area (else
+     `HITS_FIXTURE`).
+   The part of the disc inside the stock is stock as any other. The swath
+   test of K4 stays as it is: a sample that is not in the air must be
+   within 0.9 tool radius of a cut already made (else `UNCUT_STOCK`). The
+   swath test reads only the centre, so it applies to a centre in the
+   band as to any other centre.
+   Dropped: the old ring links' `AIR` meaning ("outside the stock by
+   0.1 r counts as air"). Such a centre cuts 0.9 r into stock that no cut
+   has cleared. Also dropped: a test of the distance to the part wall
+   loops. It is not exact (a wall loop is not the part), and the part zone
+   is exact.
+2. **The region keeps the part zone.** `PlanarRegion` has a new field: the
+   part grown by the tool radius plus the stock to leave. The region
+   builder sets it for an `Outside` region (`with_part_zone`, crate
+   private); it is empty else. Why: the old region did not know the part
+   outside the stock. A part can touch the stock edge or reach out of it,
+   or a second chain of the selection can lie outside the stock. Then a
+   centre in the band or in the air can be nearer to the part than the
+   tool radius plus the leave, and no value of the region showed it.
+   A region that `PlanarRegion::new` makes (not the builder) has no part
+   zone, and so no edge band: the proof refuses there as before.
+3. **The air leaves out the part zone.** The air was the band between the
+   stock grown by one and by two tool radii, less the keep-out. A part that
+   reaches out of the stock was in that air, and a link in the air could
+   run across it (the old proof accepted each sample in the air). The air
+   is now also less the part zone. The pin
+   `a_link_beside_a_part_that_reaches_out_of_the_stock_is_refused` holds a
+   link in the air across such a part. Where the part is inside the stock
+   (all the present fixtures), the air does not change. The entry stage
+   reads the same air: its room gets smaller only beside such a part.
+4. **The edge route can walk along the air.** The third try of the link
+   (a walk along a loop) now also takes the loops of the air. An end
+   joins an air loop when it stands within the edge band of it (one tool
+   radius plus the room tolerance: an end on the stock edge is one tool
+   radius from the air). The walk goes out through the band, along the
+   air, and back in. Each chord is proved as before. Centre walks are
+   shorter and come first.

+Outside) and the motion pin

+## #4254 - Path kernel K4c: an Outside piece starts at the stock edge with a proved approach from the air
+
+Follow-up of K4b (#4241, `docs/decisions/4241-kernel-link-edge-band.md`,
+"What can remove these lifts") and of K4 (#4177). Sub-PR of
+`side/path-kernel`. No old planner changes and no planner calls the new
+code yet: with the default switch the output is identical.
+
+**What was decided**
+
+1. **The approach is the last stretch of a stay-down link, not a new
+   step.** A link from the end of one piece to the start of the next can
+   end with an approach from the air: a straight stretch from a place of
+   the air to the start of the next piece. The hop is `Hop::Stay`, so the
+   plan has no new step kind and the transition table of `Plan::new`
+   stays the one gate (cut end, stay link, ready, cut). The link stage is
+   the only stage that makes a stay hop, and it makes one only when each
+   stretch of the path is proved: the stretches before the approach by
+   the chord proof of K4 (#4177, #4241), the approach by the proof below.
+   A move that has neither proof is a lift with the named reason of the
+   straight link, as before.
+   Dropped: a lift-free re-entry step in the plan (`Step::Approach` or an
+   entry without a lift). It needs a new row in the transition table and
+   a second gate for the same move, and the entry stage would then prove
+   a move that starts at depth in the cut plane, which is the link
+   stage's work.
+2. **The proof of the approach** (`link/approach.rs`). The next cut must
+   be an open piece whose start is on a stock edge loop of the region
+   (within the room tolerance). The approach starts at the place of an
+   air loop nearest to the start, within the edge band of it (a tool
+   radius and the room tolerance). The approach holds when:
+   - each sample is in the air or in the edge band (out of the part
+     zone), more than a tool radius from each keep-out area, and not
+     inside the cutter-centre area: the tool comes from outside the stock;
+   - the stretch holds in the legal room of the entry stage
+     (`entry::legal_room`), as the lead of an air entry does;
+   - it crosses no cut made and no stay link before it, and touches no
+     planned cut away from the ends of the link (`CROSSES_CUT` test of
+     K4);
+   - **the disc swept along it cuts no stock off the planned curve**: the
+     swept disc, less the swath of the next piece (the disc swept along
+     that piece), lies within one tool radius of the air. The air starts
+     one tool radius outside the stock, so no point inside the stock is
+     that near to it: the rest is outside the stock. So each piece of
+     stock that the approach cuts is cut by the next piece too, and the
+     tool begins to cut along the planned curve.
+   The area test is exact polygon geometry (`Region::sweep`,
+   `difference`). Its only tolerance is the polygon flattening: both
+   covers are grown by twice `ROOM_TOL` (10 um), because the swept discs
+   and the grown areas are each flattened within `ROOM_TOL`. No strip of
+   uncut stock is open by a constant (the defect that the review of
+   PR #4234 found).
+3. **The way to the air is a link as any other.** The path to the door
+   of the approach uses the three tries of K4 (`proof::tries`, the code
+   of `stay_path` made reusable): the straight chord, back along the cut
+   just made, a walk along a loop of the centre area or of the air. The
+   approach is the fourth try of the link, after those three to the start
+   itself fail. Shorter, proved centre walks still come first.
+4. **The order stage needs no new rule.** The start of an open piece is
+   fixed by its direction (climb or conventional, the start side's
+   sense): the order may not reverse a piece to reach another end
+   (law 3 and the direction choice). A ring cut open at the stock edge
+   has its two ends on the stock outline, so the start that the
+   direction gives is an end that the air reaches. The walk already asks
+   the link stage for a proved path to each of its first 16 starts
+   (`link::proved_path`), and that path now includes the approach. So the
+   walk takes the piece whose approach is proved, in its present order
+   of preference.
+5. **A piece whose start is not on the stock edge keeps the present
+   rule.** A closed ring, a piece that starts inside the stock or in the
+   edge band, and a start on a loop that is a part wall (a part that
+   touches or leaves the stock) get no approach. Where no proof holds the
+   lift stays with the reason of the straight link.

+## #4269 - Path kernel K6a: the converter from a kernel plan to a toolpath
+

+**What was decided**
+

+## #4406 - Path kernel law suite: each law assertion can break, and a refusal is never held
+
+Review of PR #4383 (2026-11-27, class A). Taken unattended; the rule of
+the class is the reviewer's.
+
+**What was decided**
+
+1. **A refusal is a verdict of its own.** `kit::LawVerdict` carries an
+   `Outcome`: `Held`, `Broken`, or `Refused(reason)`. A `Measure` can be a
+   refused or unread leg (`Measure::refusal`, `Measure::unread`). `judge`
+   gives `Broken` when a read measure is above its limit, else `Refused`
+   when a leg was refused or unread or when there is no measure, else
+   `Held`. `refused_held` (a refusal as 0 against 0) is removed; its callers
+   use `kit::refused`. Before, an empty measure list was held ("nothing to
+   measure"); now it is refused.
+2. **The law runner fails a refusal that is not registered.**
+   `registry::KindRecipe` has `refusals: Vec<ExpectedRefusal>` (a case name
+   and the exact reason). `law_failures` lists each broken verdict and each
+   refused verdict whose reason the kind did not register for that case.
+   `each_moved_kind_obeys_every_law` asserts that the list is empty. An
+   expected refusal never hides a broken law.
+3. **Each check, leg by leg.**
+   - L1: the first call gives the base. A refused base is refused; a later
+     call that refuses against curves is broken. Two refusals are never
+     compared by their reason text (the review note: the stand-ins share
+     one reason), so the limit of the old match is gone, not documented.
+   - L2: a region that refuses one material side is broken; both sides
+     refused is refused. A side flip that the kit cannot build is broken.
+     The order leg is never skipped; the order refused for both regions is
+     refused.
+   - L3: each side refused is refused; one side refused where another
+     plans is broken (as before); a run with no curve is unread.
+   - L4: a guide with no curve, or an entry verdict with no entry, is
+     unread.
+   - L5: an `IntoMaterial` descent onto material is read. It must move in
+     the plane by one grid cell or more (a helix or a ramp), or be a plunge
+     that the user asked for. Else it is a plunge named as a helix or ramp:
+     broken, measured by its fill. The stand-in helix (`standins::helix`)
+     was a one-point descent (a plunge with the name of a helix); it is now
+     one turn of radius half the tool radius. A plan with no entry is
+     unread.
+   - L6: the report row "the highest read ae/D" (always held) is dropped;
+     the highest read is in the place text of each cut row. A plan with no
+     cut is unread.
+   - L7: the record comes from a file, not from the run under test (see 4).
+     An empty record against an empty plan is unread; an empty record and a
+     refused run is refused with the kernel's reason; an empty record
+     against cuts is broken (count differs).
+   - Link rule: a region that is not planar makes the stay-link leg a
+     refusal, not a skipped leg.
+4. **L7 in this crate reads a recorded file.** The old holds test
+   compared the kernel with its own output of the same run. The real L7
+   record is the old planner's output; its goldens are in `camcraft-motion`
+   (`tests/pass_start_levels/kernel_baseline/`, `tests/golden/kernel_*`),
+   and the old-against-new comparison is at the motion level
+   (`tests/kernel_laws/`). The kernel crate cannot depend on motion. So the
+   stand-in kind's record is a file, recorded one time from the stand-in
+   planners and kept in `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/records/`
+   (`square_pocket.txt`, `pocket_with_an_island.txt`). The square record
+   can be checked by hand: the 16 mm centre square from (2, 2), ten rings
+   0.8 mm apart, the innermost first. The test reads the
+   file and does not write it. A change of the stand-in output, or of the
+   kernel types and the geometry under it, now breaks `l7_holds_against_the_recorded_file`
+   and the registry runner. There is no `WRITE_GOLDEN` switch: a new record
+   is a hand edit that a reviewer reads.
+5. **The proof.** Each law has a stand-in that breaks it (in its law file,
+   as before, plus `HiddenPlunge` for L5 and `no_outside` for L2) and a
+   stand-in that always refuses, reported as refused (`refusals.rs`). The
+   test `no_law_is_held_on_an_always_refusing_planner_set` runs every check
+   on a planner set where each stage refuses, and on a case whose region
+   refuses: no law is held, each law except L7 is refused, and L7 is
+   broken (the record has cuts, the kernel refused).
+6. **No change in `crates/pathkernel/src`.** Each check reads the public
+   API. The geometry helpers of `kit.rs` moved to `kit_geo.rs` (the
+   400-line law); `kit` re-exports them.
+
+7. **Old passes that were hollow (findings).**
+   - `guide_laws.rs`: the medial planner, the circle rings and the helix
+     planner "held" L2 only because their fixture regions had no stock.
+     The real region stage refuses the Outside side by name ("an Outside
+     material side needs the stock: the area outside the selection has no
+     limit"), and L2 read that refusal as 0 against 0. With the new rule L2
+     broke (measured inf against 0). The fixture now gives a stock box (10
+     mm plus four tool radii at each side), and L2 is measured and holds.
+     No kernel source changed.
+   - The stand-in helix of `standins.rs` was a one-point descent (a plunge
+     with the name of a helix). The L5 check now catches such a descent
+     (`l5_breaks_for_a_plunge_into_material_named_a_helix`).
+   - The L6 breaker pin read 0.9 or more on the full-width first ring. The
+     helix now clears the centre of that ring, and the worst unnamed read
+     is a ring corner at ae/D 0.711 against the cap 0.625. The pin now
+     asks for more than 0.7; the check did not change.
+   - The link rule skipped a stay link with no sample (a hop of zero
+     length). It now reads the points of such a hop.
+   - The registry has no moved kind yet, so `each_moved_kind_obeys_every_law`
+     ran nothing before and runs nothing now. The runner itself is pinned
+     by `the_law_runner_fails_a_kind_whose_stage_refuses_a_case`.
+
+**What was dropped**
+
+- Dropping the L7 holds test: the check would then have no test that it
+  can hold on a real plan. A recorded file is the form that the record
+  names ("golden `.cl` recorded on the head before the step").
+- Moving L7 to `crates/motion/tests/kernel_laws/` in this PR: the
+  old-planner comparison already lives at the motion level, and the
+  kernel crate keeps a check that can break.
+- Counting a refusal as "held with a note": a refused law is a legal
+  result of the kernel (Prime Directive), but it is not evidence that the
+  law holds.
+- A `NotMeasured` outcome apart from `Refused`: the runner treats the two
+  the same (only a registered reason passes), so one outcome with the
+  reason is enough.
+
+**Cost to change later**: a check is one function in one file; an outcome
+is one enum. A new record file is one text file.
